sense.text: We are covering wars and rumours of wars, and the fifth angel sounding. “And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars”: Christ is speaking with the apostles. A rumour of war is something spoken by all the people that has not occurred yet; many people speak about World War III or Armageddon, but they have not occurred as of yet. “See that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.”

“For nation shall rise against nation”: race against race. “And kingdom against kingdom”: country against country. “And there shall be famines, and pestilences”: pestilences are diseases. “And earthquakes, in divers places.”

“And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour”: John the revelator was on the island of Patmos, a salt mine; he was in prison, and Christ came and spoke to him, revealing things which were going to come to pass. “And I saw the seven angels which stood before God; and to them were given seven trumpets”: now we go over to chapter 9 and the fifth angel that sounded.
“And I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth”: this star refers to an angel. “And to him was given the key of the bottomless pit”: that him is the star. The bottomless pit is Europe.

“And there arose a smoke out of the pit, as the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by reason of the smoke of the pit”: this is talking about war. Verse 2 lets us know that war is in session; now we want to find out what war it is talking about.

precepts.why: The bottomless pit is Europe. “But now they that are younger than I have me in derision”: they that are younger than I is Esau. Younger than I means less than us; although Esau came out first, the elder shall serve the younger, and we are the chosen, God’s heirs. “Whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock”: the prophet Job is saying they weren’t good enough to sit with his dogs. “Fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste”: this tells you the time. “They were driven forth from among men”: this particular race was driven forth from among men. You look for Neanderthals and cavemen nine million years ago; this is talking about the Dark Ages. In the time of Genesis, Esau was the first dukes of Edom and they were rich, so this is another time period. “(They cried after them as after a thief;)”: we drove them from society like they stole something. “To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks”: the Caucasus mountains of Georgia and Russia, that area of Europe. Europe has very few resources and minerals; that’s why they go to places like Africa to get them. The caveman was not in the time of Genesis; Job was prophesying something that was to come. “They were children of fools, yea, children of base men”: the lowest men on earth. “They were viler than the earth.”
A precept to show you this is war; he uses the same wording about destruction. “And, lo, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace”: Sodom and Gomorrah had just been destroyed.

sense.text: “And there came out of the smoke locusts upon the earth”: these locusts make reference to planes. This is making reference to World War I. “And unto them was given power, as the scorpions of the earth have power”: a scorpion stings you from its tail, from the rear. Behind the pilot sat the rear gunner, who shot from the rear of the plane; that’s how these planes operated.

“And it was commanded them that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree”: don’t locusts eat grass, green things and the leaves on trees? These are not real locusts; John is talking about something that looked like locusts. “But only those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads”: the locusts are the nations of World War I: Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria and the Ottoman Empire, against Great Britain, France, Russia, Italy, Romania, Japan and the United States of America. These nations don’t have the seal of God. During World War I the British government issued the Balfour Declaration in 1917, announcing support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine; a homeland for European people who were converts to what was called Judaism. It was addressed to Lord Rothschild; Roth is German for red, and child is shield, red shield. The zionists and all those nations don’t have the seal of God in their foreheads.

“That they should not kill them, but that they should be tormented five months”: World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918, a five-year war; the five months make reference to five years. “And their torment was as the torment of a scorpion, when he striketh a man”: the gunner was in the rear of the plane.
“And in those days shall men seek death, and shall not find it”: about 20 million soldiers were injured, lamed, who did not die. A lot of people died, but this goes to those that were wounded.

precepts.why: One of the plagues of Egypt mentioned locusts, but there is a difference between the locusts of Exodus 10 and the locusts of Revelation 9. “That they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left”: see what locusts do. “And there remained not any green thing in the trees, or in the herbs of the field.”
“And smite Egypt with plagues, as before, and will destroy all the land thereof”: Esdras was during the Persian captivity, so Esdras ain’t talking about ancient Egypt.

Who got sealed with the seal of God: “And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” The nations these locusts make reference to don’t have the seal of God.
What that seal is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.”

Paul discussed the seal too. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: the law going into our mind is what being sealed is. The men that don’t have the seal of God are these other nations, the locusts.

sense.text: “And the shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared unto battle”: a horse prepared for battle has on armour, and these planes were made out of metal. “And on their heads were as it were crowns like gold”: their helmets, as they reflected the sun, were like gold. “And their faces were as the faces of men”: John is looking at men’s heads sticking out of the tops of the planes. He had never seen anything like this before; he is trying to describe it the best he could.

“And they had hair as the hair of women”: the long scarves they wrapped around their necks as they flew, flowing in the back; a yellow scarf looks like blonde hair. “And their teeth were as the teeth of lions”: the teeth they painted on the sides of the planes. Those planes came about at the beginning of World War II, so John is looking at an amalgamation of things happening with war. The Balfour Declaration of 1917 had not yet given them their homeland; after World War II, on 14 May 1948, the State of Israel was proclaimed by David Ben-Gurion, and they brought Europeans there, zionists who practised Judaism, converts. This is all man’s doing; it is not when God says in the scriptures that he will put the people in the land.

“And they had breastplates, as it were breastplates of iron; and the sound of their wings was as the sound of chariots of many horses running to battle”: the way these locusts fly, they sound like many chariots running to battle. The Red Baron clip showed the World War I planes with double wings, the faces of men and the scarves. In World War I the guns were not in the front, because shooting from the front damaged the propellers; the movie is Hollywood.

“And they had tails like unto scorpions, and there were stings in their tails”: the tail gunner or rear gunner sat in the back of the plane like a scorpion. “And their power was to hurt men five months”: five years.

“And they had a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit”: the messenger of Europe. Kaiser Wilhelm II, the last German Emperor and King of Prussia, initiated World War I; he reigned from 1888 until his abdication on 9 November 1918, shortly before Germany’s defeat. “Whose name in the Hebrew tongue is Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath his name Apollyon”: the same meaning, destroyer, but two different names. Some Israelites say your name cannot translate into another language; this tells you a name does change in another language.

precepts.why: What Daniel said about this, all of which occurred between World War I and World War II. “And in those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south”: the king of the south was the Ptolemies. “Also the robbers of thy people”: in the time of Christ you had the Herodians, Agrippa, certain families who had converted to what is called Judaism today. “Shall exalt themselves to establish the vision”: now we got the home, this is our homeland, we the Jews. “But they shall fall”: that’s the prophecy. No matter what they do to Israel, the scripture says they shall fall. This ain’t hate speech; we love to read the Bible.

“There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea”: how was Herod the king of Judah? The Zondervan Bible dictionary calls the Herods Idumean rulers of Palestine, and Idumean means pertaining to Edom. Herod was an Edomite. Antipater was made procurator of Judea by Julius Caesar; they made this Edomite, Herod the Great, king of the Jews. His son Herod Antipas killed John the Baptist and was called a fox by Christ, and when you called somebody a fox in them days, that was an insult. Herod Agrippa I killed James the apostle, and Paul appeared before Herod Agrippa II.

This is the Agrippa that Paul met; he was an Idumean, a convert to what they call Judaism. “Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews”: how was Herod an expert in our customs? Because he went to the schools we had set up.

“And Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul”: these Israelites were brought up with Herod the tetrarch and Saul, whom we call Paul today; they all went to the same school. Herod was in our school to learn our customs and our language and answer the questions among the Jews. That made the Herodians better vassals of Rome, to sit on the throne and govern us.

sense.text: “One woe is past; and, behold, there come two woes more hereafter”: write this down, the next woe is recorded in Revelation 11:14 and the next in Revelation 12:12. Arthur Koestler, of the people that call themselves Jewish, researched his lineage and wrote The Thirteenth Tribe in 1976. Its thesis is that the Ashkenazi Jews are not descended from the historical Israelites of antiquity, but from the Khazars, a Turkic people who converted to Judaism in the 8th century, during the Dark Ages, and migrated westwards into Eastern Europe in the 12th and 13th centuries as the Khazar empire collapsed. The Khazars are the clifts of the rocks we read about in Job 30, the Caucasus mountains. These are the people the Balfour Declaration was about, and that set up the State of Israel on 14 May 1948; this all connects. Look for the early editions; the new editions took things out.

precepts.why: “The second woe is past; and, behold, the third woe cometh quickly.”
“Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time”: we are in that period right now.

sense.text: “Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates”: the Euphrates is one of the rivers mentioned in Genesis 2. It goes through Baghdad, from Iraq near Kuwait up through Syria towards Turkey.

“Which were prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year”: a particular hour, on a particular day, a particular month and a particular year. “For to slay the third part of men”: the third part of men is the sons of the wicked; that is their purpose. God created these four and bound them there, set up just for that region, like the demon Asmodeus that was bound in Egypt in Tobit.

“And the number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand”: this is not one military, it is multitudes of militaries together prepared for battle. An article on the world’s biggest armies listed China, the USA, India, North Korea, Russia, Pakistan, South Korea, Iran, Turkey and Vietnam by active personnel.

precepts.why: We went over this a few months ago. “And the water thereof was dried up”: there are dams set up along it in recent times, and Ethiopia and Egypt are at odds over those dams. “That the way of the kings of the east might be prepared.” “And I saw three unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouth of the dragon”: that is politics, democracy and republicanism (Revelation 13:11-13). “And out of the mouth of the beast”: an economic system, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, both run from Washington DC; you got to follow America’s policies to do world business (Revelation 13:16-18). “And out of the mouth of the false prophet”: Christianity (Revelation 13:14-15). “For they are the spirits of devils”: politics, economics and Christianity are the three things that cause nations to go to war, because devils set all three systems up. Sierra Leone has diamond mines everywhere but their money is garbage; the IMF and the World Bank dictate that, and they do that through the entire continent of Africa, taking the gold and diamonds to Europe and America. “To gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.”

About this huge army. “Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, which are from the rising of the sun, from the south, from the east, and Libanus”: Libanus is Lebanon. “To turn themselves one against another”: this hasn’t happened yet; that is what the sixth angel sounding at the Euphrates is about. “And repay the things that they have done to them.” Who is them? “Like as they do yet this day unto my chosen, so will I do also, and recompense in their bosom.” Black people in church say we got to pray that there’s no war. No; God said I’m doing this for what they did to my chosen, the Israelites. We are on the brink of it now, in the starting stages, so you would be a fool to pray against it. If a missile comes and I get killed, I’m going to get raised again.
Who is God’s chosen? “O ye seed of Israel his servant, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.”

sense.text: “And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and them that sat on them, having breastplates of fire”: these are the weapons, the military instruments, their tanks, their planes, their missiles. “And the heads of the horses were as the heads of lions”: meaning they had power, and they made a sound. “And out of their mouths issued fire and smoke and brimstone”: he is describing missiles. Part 1 of the class ends here.
